phases.name: Live trip ingress and privacy
phases.description: Establish a trip-scoped, low-overhead location path before calculating ETAs.

phases.name: Location events and current state
phases.description: Validate noisy positions, retain current trip state, and preserve history asynchronously.

phases.name: Routing and adaptive ETA
phases.description: Combine route and traffic signals with prediction, then return changing ETAs.

phases.name: Scale and operational feedback
phases.description: Keep the design observable and scale by measured active-trip load.

steps.title: Start with the two mobile actors
steps.content: The brief names drivers and riders, but does not specify geography, update cadence beyond ‘every few seconds,’ a percentile latency target, retention, or trip volume distribution. Treat these as design inputs to clarify rather than inventing numeric SLOs. The same mobile surface can send driver positions and receive a trip-scoped rider view.

steps.title: Add the mobile client
steps.content: The brief calls for location updates every few seconds. The client owns permission prompts and battery-aware sampling; adapt sampling to movement and trip state rather than using an aggressive fixed polling loop. The server remains authoritative for trip membership and access.

component.label: Driver & Rider Mobile Apps

properties.purpose: Send driver location while a trip is active, receive rider-visible location and ETA updates, and adapt sampling to movement, trip state, and device battery.

component.highlightReason: The client controls location permission and battery cost; it must not be treated as a trusted authorization boundary.

steps.title: Put a regional traffic entry point in front
steps.content: A load balancer distributes long-lived real-time connections across healthy gateway instances. The brief does not require a particular transport; WebSocket or another bidirectional transport is a design choice to validate against reconnect and mobile-network behavior.

component.label: Regional Connection Load Balancer

properties.purpose: Distribute trip API and persistent location-sharing connections across healthy gateway instances; drain connections gracefully during deployment.

component.highlightReason: Connection distribution and graceful draining support a large active-trip population without assuming a specific deployment platform.

steps.title: Connect mobile traffic to the entry tier
steps.content: Keep transport termination and client retry behavior at the edge. Reconnects should be idempotent and should resume only the caller’s authorized trip view.

connection.label: Trip API + live connection
connection.description: Authenticated HTTPS requests establish or resume the real-time trip channel.

steps.title: Add the API gateway
steps.content: The gateway validates request shape, applies coarse abuse controls, and routes trip APIs separately from location-event ingestion. It should preserve streaming behavior rather than buffering updates.

component.label: Trip & Location API Gateway

properties.purpose: Validate trip and location requests, route real-time traffic, enforce transport-level limits, and keep location-sharing responses streaming.

component.highlightReason: A single controlled entry point makes the real-time path and access checks explicit.

steps.title: Connect the gateway
steps.content: The gateway is the only public application entry in this sketch; internal services are not directly exposed to mobile clients.

connection.label: Forward trip traffic
connection.description: The regional balancer forwards healthy HTTPS and persistent-connection traffic to the gateway.

steps.title: Make trip membership the privacy boundary
steps.content: Authorize each read and publish against the active trip and actor role. Do not authorize from a client-supplied trip ID alone; revoke access when a trip ends or sharing is disabled.

component.label: Trip-scoped Authorization

properties.purpose: Authenticate driver and rider identities and authorize location/ETA reads and publishes only for active trips with explicit sharing permissions.

component.highlightReason: Location is sensitive; every subscription and reconnect needs a server-side trip and role check.

steps.title: Add the trip orchestrator
steps.content: Keep trip lifecycle, authorization decisions, route selection, and the client-facing contract in an application service. Separate event processing so a burst of position updates does not block trip API work.

component.label: Trip Orchestrator

properties.purpose: Manage trip lifecycle and route policy, authorize trip-scoped location sharing, request ETA recomputation, and return the current trip view.

component.highlightReason: This owns the business workflow while streaming and historical processing remain separate concerns.

steps.title: Route authorized trip calls
steps.content: Keep identity checks on the request path and pass a server-verified actor/trip context downstream.

connection.label: Authenticate & authorize
connection.description: The gateway obtains a verified identity and trip-scoped permission before serving location data.

steps.title: Connect authorized requests to trip logic
steps.content: Only authorized callers can create or inspect a trip. The orchestrator remains the source of trip state, not a client cache.

connection.label: Verified trip context
connection.description: Trip operations receive the authenticated actor and permission result.

steps.title: Keep trip commands and position events distinct
steps.content: Location telemetry is high-volume and can be coalesced or processed asynchronously; trip creation, sharing changes, and authorization are transactional commands. Use separate paths so telemetry pressure cannot silently weaken privacy or trip-state correctness.

steps.title: Add a durable location-event stream
steps.content: Partition events by trip or another stable trip-local key so each trip can be processed in order. Retention and replay policy are open requirements; do not infer a history duration from the prompt.

component.label: Trip Location Event Stream

properties.purpose: Buffer and distribute accepted, trip-scoped location events to live-state, ETA, and historical consumers with per-trip ordering where supported.

component.highlightReason: A stream isolates frequent updates from synchronous trip APIs and supports multiple consumers.

steps.title: Publish only validated location events
steps.content: The gateway checks schema, timestamps, and trip authorization before accepting an event. Apply idempotency and stale-event handling so retries do not rewind a trip’s latest position.

connection.label: Validated location events
connection.description: Authorized, validated position updates enter the asynchronous per-trip stream.

steps.title: Interpret noisy GPS before using it
steps.content: Map matching and plausibility checks reduce GPS jumps, but preserve raw measurements and confidence so downstream ETA logic can distinguish uncertain observations from road-constrained estimates.

component.label: Location Validation & Map Matching

properties.purpose: Deduplicate and order location events, detect stale or implausible GPS jumps, map-match with confidence, and emit trip-state changes for ETA updates.

component.highlightReason: Separating noisy sensor handling from the prediction model makes GPS uncertainty explicit.

steps.title: Feed the location processor
steps.content: The consumer can scale with partition load, but a per-trip ordering key is needed to avoid applying an older point after a newer one.

connection.label: Ordered trip updates
connection.description: The stream processor consumes trip-keyed updates for validation and map matching.

steps.title: Store the latest trip view separately
steps.content: A short-lived current-state cache supports frequent reads and fanout, while durable trip and traffic history belongs in persistent storage. The frozen brief suggests geospatial indexing; add a separate active-location index only if spatial lookup is needed, while trip ID remains the canonical state key. Cache expiry must follow trip lifecycle and privacy policy; the prompt does not set a TTL.

component.label: Current Trip State Cache

properties.purpose: Serve the latest authorized trip position and ETA for low-latency reads; optionally maintain a separate spatial index for active-location queries; expire or invalidate entries when sharing ends or the trip closes.

component.highlightReason: A purpose-limited cache reduces repeated reads without making ephemeral location data the durable source of truth.

steps.title: Persist history for traffic learning
steps.content: Persist the history needed for route/traffic analysis under an explicit retention and privacy policy. Separate personally identifying trip data from aggregates where possible; no retention period is specified in the brief.

component.label: Trip & Traffic History

properties.purpose: Persist trip-scoped location samples and derived traffic observations for authorized operations and historical traffic analysis under a defined retention policy.

component.highlightReason: Historical observations improve traffic estimates, but durable storage increases the privacy and retention obligations.

steps.title: Update current state and durable observations
steps.content: The processor updates the latest trip view and sends the necessary samples to history/traffic storage. Apply retention, deletion, and trip-close behavior consistently across both stores.

connection.label: Latest validated state
connection.description: Map-matched, ordered updates replace the current trip snapshot used by live reads.

steps.title: Retain history without blocking sharing
steps.content: Historical writes can be batched or consumed asynchronously; derive time- and area-level traffic aggregates with trip identity removed or separated under the privacy policy. A history-store slowdown should not stop a rider from seeing the latest authorized location.

connection.label: Traffic observations
connection.description: Validated observations are persisted for historical traffic integration, decoupled from the live-update read path.

steps.title: Treat routing as a replaceable strategy
steps.content: The prompt requires multiple routing algorithms and traffic-aware ETAs but names no provider, region, or route-selection policy. Keep the adapter boundary replaceable and compare candidate routes using current traffic and trip context; provider outages need a declared fallback policy.

steps.title: Add the routing and traffic adapter
steps.content: This service hides provider-specific map APIs and exposes route alternatives, travel-time estimates, and traffic freshness to the trip workflow. Keep algorithm selection configurable rather than binding every trip to one routing strategy.

component.label: Routing & Traffic Adapter

properties.purpose: Call replaceable routing/traffic providers, expose alternative route algorithms, and report route, traffic freshness, and provider confidence to ETA calculation.

component.highlightReason: No dedicated map-provider catalog node exists, so this application adapter represents the integration without inventing a new component type.

steps.title: Add the ETA predictor
steps.content: Blend route/traffic estimates with recent trip progress and calibrated prediction features. A model output is an estimate, not a guarantee; retain a deterministic route-time fallback and expose confidence when inputs are stale or uncertain.

component.label: ETA Prediction Model

properties.purpose: Estimate arrival time from route alternatives, traffic conditions, trip progress, and input confidence; support model evaluation against observed arrival outcomes.

component.highlightReason: Prediction complements routing, while explicit confidence and fallback behavior handle changing conditions and imperfect GPS.

steps.title: Request route alternatives
steps.content: The trip service owns the product decision about the route; the adapter owns provider integration and traffic freshness.

connection.label: Route & traffic alternatives
connection.description: The trip workflow requests route candidates and current traffic context through a replaceable adapter.

steps.title: Recompute from route and live state
steps.content: A route change, traffic change, or validated position can trigger recomputation. Use bounded fanout and coalesce superseded updates so a burst of GPS events does not create an unbounded prediction backlog.

connection.label: Route, traffic & confidence
connection.description: Candidate routes and traffic context become ETA model inputs.

steps.title: Let location changes request updated ETAs
steps.content: The processing path emits a recompute signal only when the new observation materially changes trip state; the threshold should be measured and is not specified by the prompt.

connection.label: Material trip-state change
connection.description: Validated progress triggers route/ETA refresh when the trip state warrants recomputation.

steps.title: Return authorized live updates
steps.content: The gateway fans out only to subscribers authorized for the trip and sends the latest state rather than replaying every intermediate position to a slow mobile client. For smooth display, the client may interpolate between recent timestamped positions, but it must stop when data is stale and never treat interpolated coordinates as measured input to ETA calculation.

connection.label: Current ETA & trip view
connection.description: The trip service publishes updated estimates to the authorized real-time connection.

steps.title: Keep the rider read path on current state
steps.content: The trip API can read current position and ETA from the cache while persistent history remains separate; authorization must happen before returning cached data.

connection.label: Authorized current trip read
connection.description: The trip workflow reads the latest location/ETA snapshot after checking trip access.

steps.title: Return the model estimate to trip state
steps.content: The predicted ETA must return to the trip workflow before it can become the rider-facing estimate. Carry the estimate timestamp and confidence so the service can reject stale output and preserve the current value when a prediction fails.

connection.label: Predicted ETA & confidence
connection.description: The model returns its route-aware estimate and confidence to the trip orchestrator for validation and authorized publication.

steps.title: Use retained traffic observations
steps.content: Feed privacy-filtered historical traffic aggregates into route scoring, alongside current traffic. Keep freshness and geographic coverage visible so stale or sparse history cannot silently override live conditions.

connection.label: Historical traffic aggregates
connection.description: The routing adapter reads retained, privacy-filtered traffic aggregates to compare route alternatives with current conditions.

steps.title: Measure the complete trip path
steps.content: Define latency percentiles, stale-position behavior, GPS confidence thresholds, history retention, and regional failover with product/operations. The brief gives qualitative constraints but not enough data to promise numeric service levels or a region topology.

steps.title: Add operational telemetry
steps.content: Track connection counts, accepted and stale GPS samples, map-match confidence, event lag, ETA recomputation rate, provider failures, cache freshness, and privacy-denial events. Alert on measured service objectives once they are agreed.

component.label: Trip & ETA Observability

properties.purpose: Measure active connections, location freshness, GPS/map-match confidence, stream lag, ETA path latency, provider health, and authorization outcomes.

component.highlightReason: The constraints are testable only when telemetry follows both the live path and asynchronous consumers.

steps.title: Observe live-state freshness
steps.content: Correlate client update time, server ingest time, and processing time to distinguish mobile sampling delay from backend queueing or map-provider latency.

connection.label: Freshness & map-match metrics
connection.description: The processor emits event lag, stale-point, and GPS-confidence measurements.

steps.title: Observe model and provider quality
steps.content: Compare predicted ETA with observed arrival time by route, region, traffic condition, and confidence; monitor external routing failures without treating a model score as ground truth.

connection.label: Prediction quality & latency
connection.description: Prediction outcomes and timing support calibration and routing-provider evaluation.
